## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` must lower-case its key before merge: `get` lower-cases every lookup, so a value stored under a mixed-case key can never be read back or expired. One optional test correction was also found.

## Changes
The pull request adds `Cache.set` to `app/cache.py` and raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds with its comment updated. It adds tests for a set/get round trip, the default TTL constant, and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`: `set` writes `self._store[key]` while `get` reads and deletes `self._store[key.lower()]`. This breaks the invariant at `app/cache.py:14`, "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` sets only the lower-case key `"alpha"`, so it passes. — Any value set under a key containing an upper-case character is unretrievable, and its entry is never deleted, so `_store` grows without bound. — Fix: Use `self._store[key.lower()]` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` in `tests/test_cache.py` to set a mixed-case key.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Assert default expiry behavior instead of the constant — If `__init__` stopped using `DEFAULT_TTL` (for example a literal `ttl=60` default), `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` still passes because it asserts only `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL == 300`. `test_entries_expire` passes `ttl=1`, so no test exercises the lifetime of an entry in a default `Cache()`. — A regression in how long a default `Cache()` keeps entries would pass the test suite undetected. — Fix: Extend `test_entries_expire` with a default `Cache()` whose entry is still returned 299 seconds after `set` and is `None` at 301 seconds.
